subject: Languages

source.title: National curriculum in England: languages programmes of study

note: Controlled paraphrases of the statutory Languages programmes of study. KS2 is the foreign-language programme; KS3 is the modern foreign-language programme. Example content marked non-statutory by the source is not represented as a statutory requirement.

KS2.summary: Listen attentively to spoken language and demonstrate understanding by joining in and responding.
Explore patterns and sounds through songs and rhymes and connect spelling, sound and meaning.
Take part in conversations, ask and answer questions, express opinions, respond to others and seek clarification or help.
Speak in sentences using familiar vocabulary, phrases and basic structures, with pronunciation and intonation that support understanding, and present ideas to audiences.
Read carefully and understand words, phrases and simple writing in the language studied.
Appreciate stories, songs, poems and rhymes in the language studied.
Broaden vocabulary and use strategies such as dictionaries to understand new words in familiar written material.
Write phrases from memory and adapt them to create new sentences that express ideas clearly.
Describe people, places, things and actions orally and in writing.
Understand basic grammar appropriate to the language, including relevant gender, verb forms, patterns and sentence-building structures, and compare these with English where appropriate.

KS3.summary: Understand the main points and detail in a range of spoken language and respond appropriately.
Speak with increasing spontaneity, fluency and accuracy, initiate and sustain conversations, ask questions and develop and justify points of view.
Understand the main points, ideas and details in a range of written texts, including authentic material where appropriate.
Write at varying length for different purposes and audiences, expressing and developing ideas with increasing independence and accuracy.
Use and manipulate key grammatical structures and patterns, develop a wide-ranging vocabulary, and apply accurate grammar, spelling and punctuation.
Translate short written texts accurately into and out of the language studied, using a range of structures and vocabulary.
Use strategies such as context, reference materials and linguistic knowledge to understand unfamiliar language and communicate effectively.
Read and respond to a variety of authentic literary texts in the language studied.
Develop understanding of the culture and wider context associated with the language and use language knowledge to support further study.
